title: The Fool’s Duel
text: “Hmph! As if I would ever permit such conditions! That grave criminal, that former knight, forgot his place and injured soldiers who are the nation’s treasure—unable to suppress his murderous impulses amid the chaos of the Waves, he committed his crime! For that crime, he awaits execution! He did not ‘save’ those demi-humans!”
“Don’t give me that! It was you lot who started doing whatever you pleased the moment Seaetto-sama died!”
The mongrel lizardman roared in fury.
“Aultcray… is that truly what you think?”
Radiating killing intent, the mongrel lizardman fixed Trash with a piercing glare. Hmm… personal grudges, it seems.
“Come now! Itsuki-dono! There is no need to entertain such nonsense! There is not a shred of truth in what that creature says!”

Even Itsuki was wearing an expression that looked suspiciously like confusion at the sight of Trash and company’s behavior, I say. It was the same look he’d had during that loop where Ren was forced into a duel—head full of nothing but doubt.
“Hey, hey, Shadow Saint, looks like a dark duel’s about to start~”
“Ugh… w-what’s going on…”
At last, Ren arrived, propped up by Kuro-chan. Bad as his condition was, it seemed even he couldn’t ignore the commotion.

“Oh! Ren-dono! Perfect timing! That Shield Hero standing there dared to reopen my dear daughter’s wounds and, spouting selfish nonsense, tried to defy our orders! Itsuki-dono is going to duel him, so please, lend your strength and help punish him!”
It seemed he was proposing they gang up together to torment Father. Was he an idiot?
“……How pointless. Are you really doing that farce again? Do as you like.”
“Wha—”
“A fool’s duel?”
“To have your discrimination laid so bare like that… sorry, but you people have gone too far. So? Naofumi, what are you thinking?”
“Nothing much. I’m just trying to free someone imprisoned for a crime that isn’t really a crime, through a duel.”
“I see… if that’s what you want to do, then do as you please. But I have no interest in it.”
And so—help me, Ren seemed to be silently pleading, glancing at Kuro-chan before turning a face to Father that begged for salvation, or so I heard.
“Got it. Ren, just rest a bit and watch.”
“Hmph, if you understand that much, then I’ll go rest, uuurp—”
And with that, Ren dashed off to throw up. Kuro-chan chased after him. Ren, do enjoy the elegant drunken bliss of a Filolial-sama to your heart’s content, I say.
“So Ren’s out. Itsuki… are you still going to keep this up?”
“Eh…? Eh, yes! Just because you say something doesn’t make it true! I’ll accept the duel properly!”

Even after hearing all that, he still sided with Trash’s faction. According to Father, the reason on Itsuki’s side was that things had reached a point where he simply couldn’t bring himself to trust me outright anymore. Something felt off, sure, but Father’s attitude rubbed him the wrong way too—something like that, apparently.
“So, Itsuki… is this a one-on-one between you and me? Or will your party members be joining in too?”
Father shot Itsuki a faintly provocative glance. Seeing it, Itsuki’s expression twisted with displeasure.
However, this duel was different from the usual in several respects. Knowing the circumstances as I did, I could tell Father was deliberately steering things toward this duel, I say.
“Itsuki-sama! Leave it to me! If I’m serious, defeating the Shield Hero will be child’s play!”

Armor—ah, right, I nearly forgot—Smoked Meat, seizing the chance, had already picked up an axe and was wearing a vile grin. HAHAHA, you’re not even worth discussing, indeed. At best you’re fit to serve as a little garnish for Father’s inevitable triumph.
“The Shield Hero, alone, against Itsuki-dono’s party! My word is absolute! Should you refuse to comply, I shall forcibly confiscate the Shield Hero’s slaves!”
“Calm down, I say.”

The silent rabbit man, veins bulging on his forehead, looked about to lunge forward, so I followed up with a Paralyze Lance to numb him further. He was twitching and convulsing, and yet he still tried to stand. Quite the guts on him. Not quite up to Big Sister’s level, but he showed promise, indeed. Still, a rabbit must maintain its cuteness at all times—one mustn’t show such a savage face to Father, now must one?
“……The more I listen in silence, the more depraved you become… You! I will not forgive this!”

A burst of killing intent erupted as the mongrel lizardman’s fury finally exceeded its limits. With a series of cracking, popping sounds, he completed the transformation only available to the mongrel lizardman purchased during the loop.
“Aultcraaaaay!”
GRAAAAH! The mongrel lizardman, now a crocodile man, charged at Trash, fist raised.
“Bhuiiiiii!?”
The Crimson Swine squealed at the crocodile man’s fury and hid behind Trash.
“So you’ve shown your true colors! Everyone! Intercept him!”
Trash didn’t retreat a single step, barking orders at the soldiers. The soldiers formed ranks in unison, standing to protect him.
“Shion.”
Father stepped forward, blocking the charging crocodile man’s path. Even as Father caught him firmly, the crocodile man still tried to push forward, aiming to strike Trash.
“Calm down. Rampaging here and now won’t get you the outcome you want.”
“Let go! If he had governed properly, like Seaetto and the Queen did, everyone in the territory would—”
“Would you abandon your precious Éclair-san over a moment’s emotion?”
“Ngh! ……Guh…”
At Father’s restraint, the crocodile man lowered his raised fist and seemed to regain some composure.
“Honestly, nothing but pointless uproar after pointless uproar, with no sign of this ever coming together. Perhaps as the master looking after you, I should order you to settle down a bit more?”
“I… myself…”
“Well, I was a little surprised, but I suppose I’ll count this as something gained in the end. Shion, quite the valiant form you’ve taken there.”
At Father’s words, the crocodile man seemed to notice the change in his own body.
“This is…”
His expression was complicated—something that couldn’t quite be called joy.
“I have… awakened to the power of blood, it seems.”
“Good to hear. In any case, hold back your anger for now and stand down. This is something I need to handle.”
At Father’s words, the crocodile man saluted and bowed his head.
“Understood. Great Shield Hero-sama.”
The crocodile man seemed resolved to endure, for now.
“Now then… it seems the slave under my care has caused an unnecessary uproar. Itsuki, let’s have that duel. One against many—such a cowardly match. I suppose ‘might makes right’ applies here?”
“I would never do something so cowardly! Your Majesty! Please, enough of this already!”
Itsuki glared at Trash and the Crimson Swine, his face twisted with rage.

“I understand you’re troubled, having your daughter humiliated and facing so many problems. But acting on emotion alone, how can anyone tell what’s just!? For the sake of your dignity, I will duel Naofumi one-on-one. Mald, you too—enough of this already.”
“Ha! ……My apologies for overstepping.”

Smoked Meat delivered those words without a shred of sincerity behind them, I say. But honestly, after everything, why insist on continuing this duel? It made me want to suspect some mysterious force was at work. Itsuki, too, had reached peak stubbornness—there was simply no other word for it but foolish. Strike the iron while it’s hot, they say, but no—he just had to remain this obstinate and troublesome to the very end, indeed.
